newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sees India-Israeli ties as cause to worry.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sees India-Israeli ties as cause to worry.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday that South Asian countries were concerned by what it called growing cooperation between India and Israel, particularly in the military field.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman, commenting on Israeli President Ezer Weizman's current visit to India, told reporters that Islamabad had been closely following developments in India-Israel relations.

"Both (countries) are nuclear or known nuclear states with tested ballistic missile capability and both states have a long history of uneasy relations with their neighbours," he said, referring to prolonged hostility between India and Pakistan and between Israel and its Arab neighbours.

"Naturally, the growing cooperation between these two countries, particularly in the...military-related fields, would be a cause of concern to the countries of South Asia," the spokesman said without elaborating on such cooperation. "So we are keeping the situation under review."
Pakistan, which like many other Islamic countries does not recognise Israel, has fought three wars with India since independence in 1947, two of them over the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir.
All three are so-called nuclear threshold states capable of developing nuclear weapons quickly and joining the "Big Five" nuclear club -- the United States, Russia, China, Britain and France.
